clue.text: With him, a doctor took notes, but was generally baffled

definitions.text: With him, a doctor took notes, but was generally baffled

parts.words: With him, a doctor took notes, but was generally baffled
parts.note: describes a famous fictional detective whose companion, Dr Watson, recorded the cases while usually failing to follow the reasoning

explanation.surface: A doctor jots things down in a consultation while remaining thoroughly puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor is Dr Watson, who narrates the Conan Doyle stories and is regularly outwitted by his friend the detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue sketches the detective of Baker Street through his note-taking but bemused medical sidekick.

clue.text: System of human life in Antarctic's cool, when organised

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some arrangement for living in a cold polar region, once it has been set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when organised' rearranges ANTARCTICSCOOL into the answer; the possessive 's counts as an S here.
explanation.definitionFit: The theory of an agreement underpinning society, as in Rousseau, is a framework for human communal life.

clue.text: City records read as poem

indicators.note: read as means the letters are pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London; a log is a written record, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Municipal archives being recited as verse.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (the City of London's postal district) plus LOG, said out loud, sounds like the name of a pastoral poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral poem in dialogue, such as Virgil's, is a classical verse form.

clue.text: Like nice suburbs, or more shady places?

definitions.text: Like nice suburbs, or more shady places?

parts.words: Like nice suburbs, or more shady places?
parts.note: describes pleasant tree-lined residential areas, and also anywhere with plenty of foliage giving shade

explanation.surface: Comparing smart residential districts with gloomier spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady' tempts a reading of dubious districts, but it means shaded by trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree-lined suburbs are described as having abundant foliage, which also casts shade.

clue.text: Why 'e don't calculate this ratio?

parts.note: the dropped-aitch answer to why he does not calculate it, 'because he can't', runs together as a trigonometric ratio

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks why someone won't work out a mathematical ratio.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'cos 'e can't' quickly in a Cockney accent and you hear a trigonometric function, the reciprocal of sine.
explanation.definitionFit: This trigonometric function is one over the sine of an angle, a ratio of triangle sides.

clue.text: Not publicising big defeat

definitions.meaning: keeping something concealed rather than making it known
a thrashing or heavy loss, as in sport

explanation.definitionFit: Concealment is keeping out of sight, and a hammering in a match is a colloquial heavy defeat.

clue.text: Another composer in queue for Don Giovanni, say

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a queue is a line of people
Jacques Ibert was a French composer; 'another' because 8 Down is a composer too

explanation.surface: A second musician waiting in line to see Mozart's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don Giovanni, say' points at Mozart's opera, but the definition is Don Juan the character, a famous rake.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Giovanni is the archetypal seducer, an example of a dissolute pleasure-seeker.

clue.text: Countersign back or sides of sample

parts.note: the back of something is its end

indicators.note: sides are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Instructions to sign the reverse of a document, or the edges of a specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides of' takes S and E, the first and last letters of 'sample'.
explanation.definitionFit: To countersign is to add a confirming signature, which is to sign on the back in approval.

clue.text: Booing Lso and brand new composer

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An orchestra jeers at a freshly fashionable composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra; 'new' rearranges BOOING, LSO and BRAND, with 'and' as a link, into the Tudor composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacobean organist who wrote 'The Silver Swan' is an English composer of the early seventeenth century.

clue.text: Fish about to expire on line? So it did

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fish goes round the other pieces

parts.note: cod is a fish

indicators.note: on in an across clue means coming after, so the second piece follows the line

parts.note: to lapse is to expire, as a licence does

explanation.surface: A fish is about to die on the end of a fishing line, and then does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So it did' refers back to the dying fish: it gave way, or fell down dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's own story ends with the fish giving out, which is to say it fell down.

clue.text: War hero ordered to join Resistance

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning commanded
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A soldier is commanded to join the underground fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Bader was a legless RAF fighter pilot of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The RAF ace who flew despite losing both legs is a celebrated wartime figure.

clue.text: Furious explosion when second-class abandoned by railway

indicators.note: abandoned means left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a bang is an explosion
B is second class, as in a B grade

explanation.surface: An outburst of rage when the cheaper carriages are dropped by the train company.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious and this word are near synonyms for being very cross.

clue.text: Offender zone, say, that's found in garden centre

indicators.note: say means spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a sinner is an offender and an area is a zone

explanation.surface: A designated place for wrongdoers turns up in a nursery for plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinner area', spoken aloud, sounds like the name of a flowering pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The flowering daisy-family pot plant is a typical item on sale at a garden shop.

clue.text: Weather improving in part of forest

definitions.meaning: said of skies when cloud or rain is going away
an open space among trees in a wood

explanation.definitionFit: Skies brighten as rain moves off, and an open glade lies within a wood.

clue.text: Vote loser? Ridiculous!

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, signalling the letters are thrown into nonsense order

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a certain politician could lose an election.
explanation.walkthrough: Franklin Roosevelt won four presidential elections, so calling him a vote loser is ridiculous; the same words rearranged give his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The four-times-elected American president is the ironic opposite of an election loser.

clue.text: Soldier at the front, no balmy place

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
to be in the lead is to be at the front

explanation.surface: A soldier up front complains that nowhere is mild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no balmy place' echoes Jeremiah's 'Is there no balm in Gilead?'; the region was famed for its balm.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical region was known for its healing balm, hence a place associated with balm.

clue.text: Odd number

definitions.meaning: the grammatical form for one thing rather than several

explanation.definitionFit: Strange means peculiar, and in grammar the form opposite plural is a number category.

clue.text: Variation in sleeping-area at home rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a dorm is a sleeping area
in means at home

explanation.surface: A change in the bedroom arrangements at home is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DORMIN backwards. The definition refers to Elgar's Enigma Variations, whose ninth is named after a biblical hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth of Elgar's Enigma Variations bears this title, so it is one particular variation.

clue.text: One Scottish island and another shortly to be seen in window

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Iona is another Hebridean island

explanation.surface: Two Hebridean islands are visible through a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts the final A from IONA.
explanation.definitionFit: This vertical bar dividing panes is a part found in a window frame.

clue.text: Went round party to secure various items

parts.note: to mix is to circulate among guests at a party
to bag is to secure or obtain

explanation.surface: Someone circulated at a gathering to collect assorted things.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellaneous assortment is a collection of different items.

clue.text: After second award, start to develop a coral island

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the one before it

parts.note: a bar is added to a medal to mark a second award of it
to bud is to begin developing, as a plant does

explanation.surface: Following a further prize, a coral reef begins to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: A bar on a medal ribbon marks that the medal has been awarded a second time; 'After' is a placement signal, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean island paired with Antigua is a low coral island.

clue.text: Bite piece of apple picked up: this one?

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means read upwards, so the run is reversed

parts.note: to nip is to bite
a pip is a seed in an apple

explanation.surface: Biting into an apple and gathering a fragment of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns NIPPIP upwards. 'this one' points back to the apple: the answer is a variety of apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A pippin is an apple variety, so it is the kind of apple the clue refers to.

clue.text: Taking over from spinner's end, inveigle into mistake

indicators.note: end means the final letter of the word is taken
put into a mistake means jumbled wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler is replaced, after coaxing a batsman into an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' takes R from 'spinner's'; 'into mistake' rearranges INVEIGLE into ELIEVING.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to take over their duty, as a fresh bowler does.

clue.text: Caught a redbreast not in tree

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: not means leave out, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: the robin is called the redbreast
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A robin is caught, not inside but out in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' removes IN from ROBIN, leaving ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is a Mediterranean tree bearing edible pods.

clue.text: In competition workers get hurt

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cup is a competition, as in the FA Cup
TU, a trade union, is a body of workers

explanation.surface: Employees suffer injury during a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up is an informal phrase for upset or distressed, so hurt in feelings.

clue.text: Tear off strip of cold skin

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a hide is an animal skin

explanation.surface: Peel a piece of chilled skin away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear off strip' looks physical, but it is the idiom 'tear a strip off', to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear a strip off someone is a British idiom for scolding them severely.

clue.text: Rule committee — it has difficulty about interrupting game

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these pieces go inside the game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the letters as written

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A ruling panel finds a problem disrupting a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a reversal here, not a container; 'interrupting' breaks open the horseback game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet Communist Party's policy-making body was the ruling committee of the state.

clue.text: How to settle drawn games immediately, as seen on TV?

definitions.text: How to settle drawn games immediately, as seen on TV?

parts.words: How to settle drawn games immediately, as seen on TV?
parts.note: a tied match could be decided by replaying it at once, but the phrase really means the action reruns shown during broadcasts

explanation.surface: A proposal for resolving drawn fixtures straight away in front of cameras.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, it is games played again right away; in fact it is the slow-motion repeats on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Television shows these immediate repeats of key moments, and literally they would be rematches played at once.
